x: At the start of the race Sheffield received a serious blow in the disqualification of Proctor who joined in an extremely fast start with his team mates Allen and Hardy and our own Harry Churcher.
The race was eagerly looked forward to, to see how the two Northerners, Allen and Hardy, would shape against Harry Churcher. Hardy soon went into the lead followed by Harry and Allen.

Our usual mob match with Surrey Walking Club coincided with the A.A.A. 10,000 metres walk at the White City and in addition to Harry and Mac being invited to compete, a number of our other members were anxious to see how Hardy and Allen, of Sheffield, would shape against our 5 miles World Record Holder.
Soon came a show of red and white hoops and Allen and Hardy took the lead. Between 5 and 6 miles Hardy was "pulled" and Allen went on to win followed by Coleman of Highgate and Harry Churcher.
Sheffield United Harriers however turned up in strength with Hardy and Allen and robbed us of the team title, Hardy collecting a gold medal by beating Harry's course record of last year.

We had no competitors in the 7 miles walk which must surely be a record for our Club which is noted for its strong walking section, and it may be that the present-day opposition of Hardy and Allen makes them think that it is not worth the effort.
A one-lap course of 10 miles favoured the very fast men, and after getting away to a good start, Hardy, of Sheffield, stayed in the lead the whole journey, followed by his clubmate, R.
Sheffield United H. scored their sixth successive win with Hardy completing the hat trick for the individual title. We had 20 starters and our first man home was McMullen in 12th position (80.32).

There were 149 starters and the Sheffield lads were soon to the front with Hardy, Holland and Allen filling the first three places. At 4 miles Syd James was 15th, Eric Hall 18th, George Checkley 30th, Hugh McGreechan 36th and Bob Newson 40th.
236 lined up for the start and Vickers and Hall were seen to be well placed shortly afterwards behind Hardy, Coleman, Hawkins, Poole and others.
Hardy and Allen of Sheffield quickly took the lead at a fast pace, followed by Stan, Coleman and Hawkins. Allen soon came under the judges ban and was disqualified.

Stan kept with Hardy and Coleman in the lead until 8-8½ mls but then dropped 5 yards or so.He recovered again and was with the leaders when they went off course after being misdirected,and lost at least ½ ml.After retracing their steps,they decided to walk back together to the stadium.
